name: Luwu

extern-type-declaration.comment: `declare extern type Name<T> extends Base with ... end` from definition files. `declare` and `with` are optional here only so the `extern type Name ... end` summaries shown in hovers highlight too -- they are required in real Luau source.
extern-type-declaration.name: meta.extern-type.luwu

signature-function-body.comment: The shared body of a bodiless function signature -- generics, parameter list, metamethod and optional-marker names.

patterns.comment: The `?` marking a trait member optional -- `expect function on_click?(self)`. Scoped like `nil` so it reads as "this member may be absent".
patterns.name: constant.language.nil.luwu

declare-function.comment: `declare function name(params): Return` -- a function with no body in a definition file. Anchored to the start of the line so an indented `declare` inside a trait body stays unhighlighted: traits spell this `expect function`.
declare-function.name: meta.function.signature.luwu

expect-function.comment: Luwu Traits: `expect function name(params): Return` -- a function an implementer must provide. A trait may mark a member optional with `?` after its name: `expect function on_click?(self, cb: Callback)`.
expect-function.name: meta.function.signature.luwu

declare-variable.comment: `declare name: Type` -- a global from a definition file. Anchored to the start of the line so an indented `declare` inside a trait body stays unhighlighted: traits spell this `expect name: Type`.

expect-variable.comment: Luwu Traits: `expect name: Type` -- a field a trait requires of its implementers, which may carry the access specifier and `const` of the field (`expect private const id: string`). The type is optional: `expect cat` means `expect cat: any`.

class-declaration.comment: A class declaration. `declare` in front marks a class that exists but has no body here -- an embedder's or a definition file's class -- and may be combined with `export`.
class-declaration.name: meta.class.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Classes: the access specifier on a class's primary constructor -- `class Account private (holder: User)` -- which qualifies the constructor rather than the class. Only a qualifier when a parameter list follows it.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.access.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Classes: a primary constructor parameter may carry the access specifier and `const` modifier of the field it implicitly declares, Kotlin-style -- `class SshKey private (public const public_key: string)`. These are only qualifiers when another name follows, so a parameter may still be named `public`, `private` or `const`.
Default value of a primary constructor parameter (`class Name(a = expr)`).
patterns.name: meta.parameter.default.luwu

patterns.comment: Not valid Luau syntax -- only used to highlight the POD-constructor field list (`class Name { field: Type, ... }`) shown in class hovers.
patterns.name: meta.table.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Traits: the traits a class implements, after its header -- `class Heading(level: number) implements Element(`h{level}`), Renderable`. An entry may take generic arguments and trait arguments.
patterns.name: meta.implements.luwu

trait-declaration.comment: A trait declaration. `declare` in front marks a trait that exists but has no body here -- an embedder's or a definition file's trait -- and may be combined with `export`.
trait-declaration.name: meta.trait.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Classes: the access specifier on a class's primary constructor -- `class Account private (holder: User)` -- which qualifies the constructor rather than the class. Only a qualifier when a parameter list follows it.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.access.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Classes: a primary constructor parameter may carry the access specifier and `const` modifier of the field it implicitly declares, Kotlin-style -- `class SshKey private (public const public_key: string)`. These are only qualifiers when another name follows, so a parameter may still be named `public`, `private` or `const`.
Default value of a primary constructor parameter (`class Name(a = expr)`).
patterns.name: meta.parameter.default.luwu

patterns.comment: Not valid Luau syntax -- only used to highlight the POD-constructor field list (`class Name { field: Type, ... }`) shown in class hovers.
patterns.name: meta.table.luwu

patterns.comment: Luwu Traits: the supertraits a trait needs its implementers to also implement -- `trait Enemy needs Npc<Character>`.
patterns.name: meta.needs.luwu

implements-list-continuation.comment: Luwu Traits: the traits a class implements, after its header -- `class Heading(level: number) implements Element(`h{level}`), Renderable`. An entry may take generic arguments and trait arguments. This copy picks the list up when it starts a line of its own, below the header.
implements-list-continuation.name: meta.implements.luwu

needs-list-continuation.comment: Luwu Traits: the supertraits a trait needs its implementers to also implement -- `trait Enemy needs Npc<Character>`. This copy picks the list up when it starts a line of its own, below the header.
needs-list-continuation.name: meta.needs.luwu

patterns.comment: A `--[[ ... ]]` / `--[=[ ... ]=]` block comment. Only its delimiters and prose are scoped as a comment, not the whole block, so code in a ```luwu / ```luau fence inside it is scoped purely as code and highlights like it would outside the comment.
Comment prose. Stops at `]`, a backtick, `@` and the markdown punctuation above so the end delimiter, fences, doc tags and markdown can still match.
patterns.name: comment.block.luwu

markdown_prose.comment: Markdown in doc comments -- `--[=[ ... ]=]` blocks and `---` lines are read as markdown, so headings, emphasis, lists, links and inline code render as such. Code fences are matched before this and highlight as Luwu/Luau instead.

patterns.comment: An ATX heading -- `# Title`.
patterns.name: markup.heading.luwu

patterns.comment: A blockquote marker.
A bullet or ordered list marker. The marker alone is scoped; the item's text is prose.
`*italic*` / `_italic_`. Guarded so a `snake_case` word or a `*` in prose is left alone.
patterns.name: markup.italic.luwu

patterns.comment: `~~struck through~~`.
patterns.name: markup.strikethrough.luwu

patterns.comment: `` `inline code` ``. Never a fence, which the rules above take first.
patterns.name: markup.inline.raw.luwu

patterns.comment: `[text](target)`.

The `read`/`write` variance modifier on an indexer -- `{ read [string]: number }`. Named properties pick theirs up in the rule below, but an indexer has no name, so it needs its own match ahead of the `[` rule.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.access.luwu
